描述_EN: beato also sold his images of china to british officers as unmounted prints with his stock number, title, and date written in pencil on the verso of each print. but even before the ‘narrative’ was constructed by the purchaser, beato himself controlled the story, determining what was considered worthy of recording and eliminating any conflicting viewpoints. accompanying the anglo-french expeditionary force, which went on to seize beijing and force the chinese empire to accede to sweeping political and economic demands, beato’s views, combining topographical and military information, provided a visual record of the imperial campaign. they were often included in ‘progress’ reports sent from hong kong to the commanding officer of the british army. by assembling a selection of images, the purchaser could construct a personal visual record. surviving albums such as this one have differing numbers of prints, and are a reflection of the owner's personal military career. having established his reputation as a professional photographer documenting military conflicts in the crimea and india during the 1850s, italian-born felice beato arrived in china in march 1860 during the final months of the second opium war. these views were absorbed by the public as part of a larger visual memory documenting england’s rise as an imperial power.
描述_ZN: 贝托还将他的中国图片作为未装裱的印刷品出售给英国军官，并在每张印刷品的背面用铅笔写上他的库存编号、标题和日期。 但即使在购买者构建 "叙事 "之前，贝托自己就已经控制了这个故事，决定什么是值得记录的，并消除了任何冲突的观点。 随同英法联军远征军攻占北京，迫使中华帝国同意全面的政治和经济要求，贝托的观点结合了地形和军事信息，为帝国的运动提供了视觉记录。 它们经常被纳入从香港寄给英军指挥官的 "进展 "报告中。 通过对图片的选择，购买者可以构建一个个人视觉记录。 像这样的存世相册有不同数量的印刷品，反映了主人的个人军事生涯。 在19世纪50年代作为专业摄影师记录克里米亚和印度的军事冲突后，意大利出生的费利斯-贝托在第二次鸦片战争的最后几个月于1860年3月来到了中国。 这些观点被公众所吸收，成为记录英国作为帝国大国崛起的更大的视觉记忆的一部分。
